headline: In a side project, engineers at the startup Axiom had OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra drive a Toyota Corolla to an In-N-Out drive-through.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: a striking real-world test; the headline matches the article, which also states its doubts.
importance_line: Robotics builders and road-safety people get an early sign that general AI models can handle physical tasks, but the honest doubt is that this was one informal test with a safety driver, and only one model finished the engineers' simple driving course.
summary: WIRED reports that three engineers at the startup Axiom had OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra, a model normally used for text and code, steer a 2024 Toyota Corolla through an In-N-Out drive-through, with a safety driver ready to brake. The models at first refused to take control and drove only after careful prompting, and on DrivingBench, a simple parking-lot course the engineers built, only Astra finished, and very slowly.
notes: Read in full from WIRED (5,729 chars). The drive was a side project outside the engineers' work at Axiom (article). Other results from DrivingBench: Claude Fable 5.1 got 45 percent of the way round the course, Grok 11 percent. Event date not stated ('recently'); article published 7 Oct 2026.
